title: LCLI-670 round-2 follow-ups: the --repo guard, the task-only coupling checks, and the untested catch (F11-F16)
description:
Follow-up from LCLI-670's round-2 review (approved at 432cf61b; PR opum-ai/lore-cli#581 merged 6ab1e32b). All non-blocking, all in the `--decision` arm LCLI-670 added. NOT held; queues right after LCLI-723.

F11 — the `--repo` guard (src/core/decision-ref.ts:89-99) rejects "", ":" and "\" but NOT "/" or whitespace. `--repo "lore cli"` writes `lore cli:DEC-1`, which DECISION_REF (decision-ref.ts:23) cannot parse back, and `--repo opum-ai/lore-cli` stores a SECOND SPELLING of the same repository, defeating the qualification. Fix: ONE shared predicate rejecting both "/" and whitespace, used by the `--repo` arm and the derived-name arm (:78) alike.

F12 — assertNoCommaInId and assertNoLabelCaseCollision (src/commands/link.ts:938-940, 976-978) run on the DOC-SIDE-ONLY `--decision` arm, so `lore link adr/0001-a,b --decision DEC-9` is refused for a Backlog LABEL reason that arm never touches (it writes no label). Skip both when decisions are present.

F13 — B2's catch branch is untested. decision-ref.ts:51 calls `Bun.spawnSync` inline rather than through the GitSpawn seam (src/state.ts:49/52). Take the seam so the throw is injectable and testable, or empty PATH around one call.

F14 — record WHY 432cf61b trimmed cli-surface: the `implementation` profile's declared capacity, and the pin-capacity rule reached through `reference/cli-contract` (LCLI-702). Belongs on LCLI-670 or here.

F15 — docs/reference/cli-contract.md:236 does not mention `decisions` in `link.result`. CAUTION: cli-contract is pinned by THREE profiles, so any growth there moves every pinning profile's budget in the same change (the LCLI-702 gate) — do it with a dev merge in the same pass, not as a lone edit.

F16 nits — `isDecisionRef` (decision-ref.ts) is exported but unused; `dedupeTaskIds`' docstring talks about task ids while it now dedupes decision refs too; the readonly mismatch at link.ts:107/113; and a redundant `require("node:fs")` at test/link-decision.test.ts:105.
plan: F11 — ONE shared qualifier predicate (non-empty, and no `:`, `\`, `/` or whitespace), used by the `--repo` arm, the derived-name arm (`repositoryNameFromRemoteUrl`) and the `memberId` arm alike. The two arms disagree today: `--repo` rejects `:`/`\` but not `/` or whitespace, while the derived-name arm rejects `/` but not whitespace. Leader ruled memberId in scope, since it writes the same qualifier.

F12 — skip `assertNoCommaInId` and `assertNoLabelCaseCollision` on the doc-side-only `--decision` arm (src/commands/link.ts:938-940, 976-978). They refuse `lore link adr/0001-a,b --decision DEC-9` for a Backlog LABEL reason that arm never touches.

F13 — give `originRepositoryName` a SYNC injectable spawner defaulting to a reuse of `GitPreflightSpawn`/`bunGitPreflightSpawn` (src/adapters/git-preflight.ts), NOT `state.ts`'s async `GitSpawn` (leader ruling): no async ripple through `resolveDecisionQualifier` and its callers, no `process.env` mutation, so it is safe on windows-latest. `state.ts` stays untouched. Tests inject a thrower to cover the catch branch.

F14 — record WHY 432cf61b trimmed cli-surface: the `implementation` profile's declared capacity and the pin-capacity rule reached through `reference/cli-contract` (LCLI-702). A tracker note, not a code change.

F15 — add `decisions` to the documented `link.result` shape (docs/reference/cli-contract.md:236), NET ZERO against the pinned capacities: cli-contract is PINNED by implementation, review and verification, so any growth moves all three budgets (LCLI-702) and no target moves (DEC-194). Same measured discipline as #586: `estimateTokens` is `ceil(length / 4)`, so pay for the addition by tightening the same section.

F16 — four nits: `isDecisionRef` is exported and referenced nowhere but its own definition (remove it); `dedupeTaskIds`' docstring still speaks of task ids though it dedupes decision refs too; the readonly mismatch at link.ts:107/113; and a redundant `require("node:fs")` at test/link-decision.test.ts:105.

Proofs, each with a mutation control: the shared predicate refuses `/` and whitespace at all three arms; the `--decision` arm accepts a comma-bearing doc id and still refuses an in-arm-invalid one; the injected throwing spawner reaches the caller's refusal rather than propagating a throw; F15's edit is measured against the pinned capacities.
implementationNotes:
F14, RECORDED 2026-10-14 (it belongs here as much as on LCLI-670, and LCLI-670 is Done): WHY 432cf61b TRIMMED `docs/reference/cli-surface.md` instead of adding to it. That page is a declared source of the `implementation` agent profile, and `reference/cli-contract` is PINNED by `implementation`, `review` and `verification`, so anything added to either grows every pinning profile's rendered capacity at once -- the rule LCLI-702 made error-tier (`agent-profile-pin-capacity`, which names each over-capacity pinning profile with its deficit). The trim was the same move this task had to repeat for F15, and it is why an edit to either page is not a free edit.

MEASURED THIS SESSION, so the rule's cost is on the record with numbers rather than as a caution: the capacity estimate is `estimateTokens = ceil(length / 4)` (src/core/bundle.ts), and `docs/reference/cli-contract.md` sits at exactly 43664 bytes = 10916 tokens -- on a 4-byte boundary, so ANY growth, even one byte, moves the rendered ceiling by a whole token for all three pinning profiles. F15's `decisions` mention therefore ships NET NEGATIVE: -4 bytes, 10916 -> 10915 tokens, paid for by tightening the edited row's own wording (the neighbouring rows are noun phrases, so the verb in "updated frontmatter refs" was also the odd one out) plus one redundant clause in the same table. `CHANGELOG.md` is NOT a declared source of any profile -- checked, not assumed -- so the user-facing entry for this task costs nothing and went there.

FOLLOW-UP FOR WHOEVER NEXT EDITS A PINNED PAGE: measure the pre-change bytes first; a page that happens to sit on a 4-byte boundary gives up a token to a single character.

CORRECTION + RULE, 2026-10-14. The F12 claim I made earlier this session -- that the case-collision half is "provably not observable through `link`" because "loadBundle folds case-colliding ids" -- was WRONG, and the way it was wrong is worth more than the fix.

WHAT HAPPENED. #588's CI run 38553241722 concluded FAILURE on head 41bca330, on the ubuntu leg only, on my OWN test: `the case-collision half cannot be observed from here` expected ["adr/0001-a"] and received ["adr/0001-A", "adr/0001-a"]. The expectation was an artifact of THIS CHECKOUT'S case-INSENSITIVE filesystem, not a property of `loadBundle`. Measured locally: writeFileSync "0001-a.md" then "0001-A.md" leaves ONE directory entry, the SAME inode, holding the second content. So the fixture never contained two files here, and I read a filesystem's behaviour as the product's. It was green on macOS and on windows-latest (NTFS collapses the pair too) and red only on the case-sensitive ubuntu runner -- the only place it could show -- and the reviewer CONFIRMED the false claim, because the reviewer's own run agreed with it. The claim was also written into the test file's comment, the #588 PR body, and my report to the leader; all three are corrected on the new head.

THE RULE, which is the part that should outlive the incident: ON THIS MACHINE, A TEST WHOSE FIXTURE DIFFERS ONLY BY CASE PROVES NOTHING UNTIL A CASE-SENSITIVE FILESYSTEM HAS RUN IT. Do not gate such a test on `process.platform` either -- APFS can be formatted case-sensitive and a Linux mount can be case-insensitive, so the platform is not the property the test needs. Probe at RUNTIME: write `probe` and `PROBE` in a temp dir and count `readdirSync` entries. Let the probe THROW if it cannot write rather than answer "no", or a broken environment silently skips the proof everywhere while looking like a considered decision.

THE FIX, on the new head. test/link-decision.test.ts now PROVES the case-collision half both ways instead of measuring why it supposedly could not: the same two ADRs, the `--decision` arm linking, and the task arm still refusing -- gated on that runtime probe, with the skip naming the probe in the test's own name. VERIFIED WHERE IT CAN ACTUALLY RUN, both ways: 29 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail on this macOS checkout (the probe reports one entry and both tests skip), and 31 pass / 0 fail in a Linux container (oven/bun:1.3.14, the image docker/e2e pins) where both tests RAN rather than skipped. The production change is untouched and stays as reviewed; only the proof of it was wrong.
finalSummary:
Delivered in PR opum-ai/lore-cli#588, squash-merged to dev. Final head 0c1d5737; CI run 38554883878 ran completed/success -- 13 pass, 1 skipped, 0 failures -- and, because a green run alone was not the bar, the ubuntu leg's log (job 115821448561) shows BOTH case-collision tests as `(pass)` with no skip marker and zero occurrences of the "SKIPPED:" marker anywhere in that log. The only real proof of that half therefore RAN on the case-sensitive runner, rather than passing as a skip.

F11: ONE `isValidQualifier` predicate (non-empty; no `:`, `\`, `/` or whitespace) at all three arms that produce a stored qualifier -- `--repo`, the name derived from `origin`, and the workspace `memberId`, which was unvalidated entirely. A name that was already acceptable is still accepted; what changed is that a bad one is no longer WRITTEN.
F12: both Backlog-label guards (comma-bearing id, case-colliding id) skipped through one `sendsLabel` predicate on the doc-side `--decision` arm, which sends no label; the task arm is unchanged and still refuses both.
F13: `originRepositoryName` takes the injectable SYNCHRONOUS `GitPreflightSpawn` seam, reusing `adapters/git-preflight.ts` rather than adding a second seam -- so the unreadable-remote catch is reachable from a test with no async ripple through `resolveDecisionQualifier` and no `process.env` mutation. `state.ts` untouched.
F14: record note on why 432cf61b trimmed cli-surface, with this task's own measurement of the rule.
F15: `link.result` names `decisions`, NET NEGATIVE against the pinned capacities -- -4 bytes, 10916 -> 10915 tokens, folded into the -4-byte result rather than a budget move. cli-contract is PINNED by implementation, review and verification; no target moved (DEC-194).
F16: the dead `isDecisionRef` export removed; the `dedupeTaskIds` docstring now states both coupling lists it serves; `LinkArgs.taskIds` readonly like its sibling; the redundant inline `require("node:fs")` dropped.

PROOFS: five mutation controls at the first head, each re-instating the pre-fix wording and reddening the predicted subset (the `--repo` arm 3, the derived-name arm 2, the memberId arm 1, `sendsLabel` 1, the F13 catch 1), baseline green.

CORRECTION, and the reason the second head exists: the first head shipped a WRONG CLAIM -- that the case-collision half of F12 was "provably not observable through `link`" because "`loadBundle` folds case-colliding ids". It does not; the claim was an artifact of the authoring machine's case-INSENSITIVE filesystem, where writing `0001-a.md` then `0001-A.md` leaves ONE inode. CI run 38553241722 reddened on the ubuntu leg only, on that test, and the claim had also reached the PR body and this record. Corrected at 0c1d5737 and replaced with a real both-ways proof (the `--decision` arm links; the task arm still refuses) gated on a RUNTIME probe that throws rather than answering "no". Verified on BOTH filesystems before pushing: 29 pass / 2 skip on macOS, and 31 pass / 0 fail in a Linux container using `oven/bun:1.3.14`, the image docker/e2e pins, where both gated tests ran.

THE RULE, recorded so it outlives the incident: ON THIS MACHINE, A TEST WHOSE FIXTURE DIFFERS ONLY BY CASE PROVES NOTHING UNTIL A CASE-SENSITIVE FILESYSTEM HAS RUN IT. Gate such a test on a runtime probe, never on `process.platform` -- APFS can be formatted case-sensitive and a Linux mount can be case-insensitive.

Follow-ups -- the three from round 1, the delta review's three, and the corrected premise -- are filed as LCLI-729.
